A1-A2.headline: The Story of the Summer Olympics

pages.text: The Summer Olympic Games are a big global sports event. They happen normally every four years. The very first modern Games took place in Athens, Greece, in 1896. Pierre de Coubertin started the group that runs them, called the International Olympic Committee.

In 1896, only 14 countries came to the Games. There were fewer than 250 competitors, and all of them were men. Women could not take part in those first events. Women first took part officially in the Paris Games in the year 1900.

Over time, the Games grew much bigger. By the 2021 Games in Tokyo, more than 11,000 competitors came from 206 nations. Almost half of these athletes were women. Countries all over the world have hosted this huge international multi-sport event.

Cities in many different countries want to host the Olympics. London and Paris have hosted the Games three times. Other places like Los Angeles, Athens, and Tokyo have hosted them twice. Hosting brings big changes and new investments to city infrastructure.

Australia, France, and Great Britain are the only countries that have won at least one medal in every single Summer Games. Great Britain is the only country to win at least one gold medal in every single edition of the event.

The United States has hosted the Summer Olympics four times in cities like St. Louis, Los Angeles, and Atlanta. The U.S. also leads the all-time medal count. The Games continue to change today, adding new sports for athletes to play. কন্যা

B1-B2.headline: History and Growth of the Summer Olympics

pages.text: The Summer Olympic Games are the world's largest and most prestigious multi-sport international event. Usually held once every four years, the modern tradition began in Athens in 1896. The International Olympic Committee, founded by Pierre de Coubertin, organized this groundbreaking global competition.

The inaugural 1896 Games featured just 42 events with fewer than 250 male competitors from 14 nations. Female athletes were initially excluded, though women officially joined the competition at the 1900 Paris Games. Participation expanded dramatically over the decades, reaching 11,319 competitors from 206 nations by 2021.

Cities worldwide have competed to host the Olympics, spreading the event across five continents. London and Paris have hosted three times, while Los Angeles, Athens, and Tokyo have hosted twice. Rio de Janeiro hosted the first South American Games in 2016 amid various local challenges.

Only three countries have won at least one medal in every Summer Games: Australia, France, and Great Britain. Furthermore, Great Britain stands alone as the only nation to secure at least one gold medal in every single edition. The United States leads the all-time medal count.

Hosting the Olympics requires massive investments in local infrastructure, playing a key role in urban development and global integration. Preparing for these massive gatherings often involves significant political, economic, and logistical efforts from the host cities and nations.

The sports programme has evolved continually since 1896. The 2024 Games featured 32 sports, while future editions plan to introduce entirely new disciplines like flag football and squash. International sports federations govern the qualification rules for each specific competition.

C1-C2.headline: Evolution of the Modern Summer Olympics

pages.text: Evolving from nineteenth-century ideals of international understanding, the Summer Olympic Games were established by Pierre de Coubertin through the founding of the International Olympic Committee in 1894. The inaugural 1896 Games in Athens inaugurated a quadrennial tradition that subsequently became the world's preeminent international multi-sport gathering.

The scope of the competition expanded exponentially from the 1896 programme of 42 events and under 250 male athletes to over 11,000 competitors across 206 nations by 2021. Although female participation was absent initially, women debuted officially in 1900, eventually comprising nearly half of all athletes in contemporary editions.

Geographically, the Games have spanned nineteen countries across five continents. Cities such as London and Paris achieved multiple hosting duties, while Rio de Janeiro marked South America's inaugural hosting milestone in 2016 amidst complex socioeconomic and health controversies.

Competitive dominance remains concentrated among specific nations. Australia, France, and Great Britain share the distinction of securing medals in every Summer Games, with Great Britain uniquely capturing at least one gold medal in every edition. The United States leads the cumulative medal standings comprehensively.

Infrastructure enhancement remains inextricably linked to hosting responsibilities, as municipal leaders leverage the Games to accelerate urban development and enhance global economic competitiveness. Such capital investments demand substantial financial commitments, exemplified by security and operational expenditures in modern editions.

The athletic programme has adapted continuously, transitioning from historical roots to include 32 sports in recent programmes and planned expansions into emerging disciplines. Governing International Sports Federations autonomously regulate qualification protocols, while the IOC categorizes sports based on global popularity metrics.
